html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Plan your time: about 90 seconds a question
  • Read a stem, and handle "most appropriate", "least" and "NOT"
  • Spot the look-alike traps and the old names
  • Use flag and review, and prepare for exam day

2Time: About 90 Seconds a Question

  • 60 questions in 90 minutes is about 90 seconds each
  • First pass: answer what you know quickly, and flag the doubtful ones
  • Second pass: use the Review Screen to return to the flagged questions
  • Keep a few minutes for a final check before you click Finish Exam
  • The timer keeps running, even during a requested break

Exam tip

Do not sink three minutes into one question: flag it and move on.

3Reading a Stem

  • Find the ask: does it define, choose, fix or compare?
  • Find the layer: workload, network, storage, security, delivery or architecture
  • Note the constraints: a cloud or bare metal, one namespace, no code change
  • Predict the answer first, then compare it with the options

Exam tip

Read the last line of the stem first: it holds the real question.

4Most Appropriate, Least and NOT

Pattern What to do
"Most appropriate" several options may work: pick the one that fits every detail of the scenario with the least extra work
"Least" pick the smallest change or permission that still works, as in least privilege
"NOT" or "EXCEPT" find the false statement: test each option as true or false
"First" look for the dependency: a Secret must exist before the Pod that needs it
"Which component" name the layer first: API server, scheduler, kubelet or proxy
Exam tip

Underline the small word that flips the question: NOT, least or first.

5Look-Alike Traps

  • Deployment or StatefulSet: interchangeable Pods, or a stable name and storage
  • Role or ClusterRole: one namespace, or cluster-wide
  • PV or PVC: the storage, or the request for it
  • Liveness or readiness: restart, or traffic
  • Ingress or Gateway API: frozen, or the successor
  • Requests or limits: they drive placement, or they are enforced

Exam tip

When two options look alike, find the one word that separates them.

6Eliminating Options

  • Remove options that name the wrong layer, such as a kubelet answer to a scheduling question
  • Be wary of absolutes such as "always" and "never": Kubernetes has exceptions
  • Remove options that are true but do not answer the question
  • Among the rest, choose the one that fits the scenario details
  • Choose an answer for every question, and change it from the Review Screen if you think again
Exam tip

Two options left? Reread the stem for the detail that separates them.

7Flag and ReviewMoving

  • Previous and Next move between questions
  • Flag a question: flagged items are highlighted on the Review Screen, where you can return and update an answer
  • At the last question, Review Exam leads to the Review Screen and Finish Exam
  • The timer shows the time left; a requested break does not stop it
  • After a disconnect, the timer does not pause, and no time can be added back
  • As of 30 October 2026: this is what the Linux Foundation handbook describes

Exam tip

Flag early, review once, finish with time to spare.

8Old Names in Older MaterialOld wording

If a question says Think
PodSecurityPolicy removed: Pod Security admission and the three Standards
dockershim removed: a CRI runtime such as containerd or CRI-O
Endpoints deprecated: EndpointSlices
The 4 Cs cloud, clusters, containers, code: the older security layers
Five domains, 46/22/16/8/8 the earlier curriculum; the current one has four
  • An old name still points to the same idea: translate it, then answer
Exam tip

Translate the name, then answer the concept.

9Exam Day: Rules and SetupMoving

Area What the Linux Foundation asks
Delivery online, proctored remotely by streaming audio, video and screen sharing
Browser the PSI Secure Browser; run the system check first, and avoid a work-provided device
Camera a webcam you can move, to show your surroundings
Room private and quiet, a clutter-free desk, clear walls, good light, the door closed
ID a valid, government-issued, original ID whose name matches your verified name
  • As of 30 October 2026: read the Linux Foundation candidate handbook before the day
Exam tip

Test your setup a few days early, not on the morning.

10Final Week Checklist

  • Review Module 15 and the labels from Module 0
  • Redo the questions you missed, and say the reason aloud
  • Check your system, your room and your ID against the Linux Foundation rules
  • Rest: a clear head earns more points than one more hour of notes
  • Remember the plan: about 90 seconds a question, flag, return, finish
Exam tip

Confidence comes from a routine you have practiced.

11Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Time about 90 seconds a question; first pass, second pass, final check
Stems find the ask, the layer and the constraints, and predict first
Patterns most appropriate, least, NOT, first, which component
Traps and names the six look-alike pairs, and the old names mapped to new
Exam day flag and review, the timer never stops, and the Linux Foundation rules for room, camera and ID
